import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Combine date and time columns and convert to datetime objects
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract hour of the day and day of the week
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour
df['day_of_week'] = df['datetime'].dt.day_name()

# Define the correct order for the days of the week for plotting
day_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
df['day_of_week'] = pd.Categorical(df['day_of_week'], categories=day_order, ordered=True)

# --- Data Aggregation for Heatmap ---
# Create a pivot table to aggregate total sales by day of the week and hour
heatmap_data = df.pivot_table(
    values='total',
    index='day_of_week',
    columns='hour',
    aggfunc='sum',
    fill_value=0
)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 9))

# Create the heatmap
sns.heatmap(
    heatmap_data,
    cmap='YlGnBu',
    linewidths=.5,
    annot=False,  # Annotations would be too cluttered
    ax=ax,
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'}
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set title and labels with appropriate font sizes
ax.set_title('Coffee Shop Peak Hours: Total Sales by Day and Hour', fontsize=20, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Improve tick label appearance
plt.xticks(rotation=0, fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(rotation=0, fontsize=10)

# --- Save the Figure ---
# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
